title: Steady-state token throughput micro-suite for core models
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build and maintain a micro-benchmark suite that measures steady-state token throughput and tail latency characteristics for our core models under realistic steady traffic. Unlike short-burst TPS probes, this suite focuses on warmed KV-cache behavior, sustained batching patterns, and p95/p99 tail dynamics over long windows (10–30 minutes). It should be lightweight to run in CI gates, reproducible locally for engineering experiments, and provide deterministic inputs for regression detection. Key goals: 1) produce consistent tokens/sec baselines for model variants and quantization configs; 2) surface p95 and p99 regressions with statistical confidence; 3) expose mode differences when cache is cold vs warmed; 4) integrate with observability to auto-open regression alerts and link to performance dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Automated benchmark (CLI) that runs for a configurable duration and outputs tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies and sample variance
Bench harness supports at least 3 model variants (fp16, int8, q4f) and CPU fallback path in private deployments
Regression detector that compares current run to rolling baseline and raises a regression if tokens/sec drops >5% with p<0.01
CI job that runs lightweight 5m steady-state profile on every model onboarding PR and blocks on regressions
Results ingest into Console performance dashboard with links from ticket and PR
updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created by Maya. Draft plan and success metrics added. Noted overlap with ENG-21456 for token stream stability; will reuse some probes but change steady-state semantics.

2025-02-12: Spike week — implemented prototype harness that produces steady-state streams and warms KV cache for 2m. Findings: warmed throughput is ~12% higher than cold baseline for small batch sizes.

2025-02-15: Design review with PM and Perf team. Decided on two modes: a lightweight CI mode (5m, single model, default batch) and an extended lab mode (30m, multivariant, variable seq lengths). Ravi to open PR with initial CLI and grafana dashboard ingestion.

2025-02-18: Uploaded draft docs and example outputs to Confluence (link in attachments). Identified trade-off: long runs increase CI cost; mitigation is to gate full runs to nightly pipeline and keep PR runs short but statistically normalized.

2025-02-19: PR #3247 opened with harness and a new regression-detector. Requesting review from @linh (observability) and @noah (runtime). Blocker: need a stable synthetic prompt distribution generator to avoid noise across runs. Assigned to Ravi.

2025-02-20: Implemented synthetic prefix generator that approximates production token lengths and entropies. Running comparison against production traces to tune distribution parameters. Next: finalize threshold math for regression detector.
